questions.q: Expand $\sin(x+30^\circ)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$, using exact values for $\sin30^\circ$ and $\cos30^\circ$.
Given $\sin A=\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $\cos B=\dfrac{12}{13}$, with $A$ and $B$ both acute, find $\cos(A+B)$.
questions.answer: Since $A,B$ are acute, $\cos A=\dfrac{4}{5}$ and $\sin B=\dfrac{5}{13}$. $\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B=\dfrac{4}{5}\cdot\dfrac{12}{13}-\dfrac{3}{5}\cdot\dfrac{5}{13}=\dfrac{48}{65}-\dfrac{15}{65}=\dfrac{33}{65}$.

questions.q: Use the compound-angle formula for tangent to find the exact value of $\tan75^\circ$, using $75^\circ=45^\circ+30^\circ$.
Use the compound-angle formula for cosine to find the exact value of $\cos15^\circ$, using $15^\circ=45^\circ-30^\circ$.
Given $\cos\theta=-\dfrac{1}{3}$ with $90^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$, find $\cos2\theta$ and state which quadrant $2\theta$ lies in.
questions.answer: $\cos2\theta=2\cos^2\theta-1=2\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right)-1=-\dfrac{7}{9}$. Since $90^\circ<\theta<180^\circ$, $2\theta$ lies between $180^\circ$ and $360^\circ$; combined with $\cos2\theta<0$ (which requires an angle between $90^\circ$ and $270^\circ$), $2\theta$ must lie in the third quadrant, i.e. $180^\circ<2\theta<270^\circ$.

sections.heading: Solving equations using double angle formulas

questions.answer: $2\sin\theta\cos\theta-\cos\theta=0\Rightarrow\cos\theta(2\sin\theta-1)=0$. So $\cos\theta=0$, giving $\theta=90^\circ$ or $270^\circ$; or $\sin\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$, giving $\theta=30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$.

questions.q: Express $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta$ in the form $R\sin(\theta+\alpha)$, with $R>0$ and $0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ$, giving $\alpha$ to the nearest degree.
Express $\sqrt{3}\sin\theta-\cos\theta$ in the form $R\sin(\theta-\alpha)$, giving exact values of $R$ and $\alpha$.

sections.heading: Using the R-form to find extrema and solve equations

questions.q: The graph shows $y=5\sin(x+53^\circ)$, the R-form of $3\sin x+4\cos x$ found earlier. State the maximum and minimum values of $3\sin\theta+4\cos\theta$, and the value of $\theta$ (to the nearest degree, $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$) at which the maximum occurs.
questions.answer: Since $-1\leq\sin(\theta+53^\circ)\leq1$, the maximum value is $R=5$ and the minimum is $-5$. The maximum occurs when $\theta+53^\circ=90^\circ$, i.e. $\theta=37^\circ$.

questions.q: Solve $\sqrt{3}\sin\theta-\cos\theta=1$ for $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$, using the R-form $2\sin(\theta-30^\circ)$ found earlier.
questions.answer: $2\sin(\theta-30^\circ)=1\Rightarrow\sin(\theta-30^\circ)=\dfrac{1}{2}$. For $\theta-30^\circ$ in the range $-30^\circ\leq\theta-30^\circ<330^\circ$: $\theta-30^\circ=30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$, giving $\theta=60^\circ$ or $\theta=180^\circ$.

Factor as a difference of squares: $\cos^4\theta-\sin^4\theta=(\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta)(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)$. Since $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$, this simplifies to $\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta$, which is exactly $\cos2\theta$.

sections.heading: Solving equations that combine several identities

questions.q: Solve $2\cos2\theta+3\sin\theta=1$ for $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$, using $\cos2\theta=1-2\sin^2\theta$, giving answers to one decimal place where needed.

questions.answer: $1-2\sin^2\theta=1-\sin\theta\Rightarrow-2\sin^2\theta+\sin\theta=0\Rightarrow\sin\theta(1-2\sin\theta)=0$. So $\sin\theta=0$, giving $\theta=0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$; or $\sin\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$, giving $\theta=30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: alternating current

questions.q: This question has three parts. The voltage in an AC circuit is modeled by $V(t)=6\sin(100\pi t)+8\cos(100\pi t)$ volts, where $t$ is time in seconds. (a) Express $V(t)$ in the form $R\sin(100\pi t+\alpha)$, giving $R$ exactly and $\alpha$ in radians to four decimal places. (b) State the maximum voltage reached, and the smallest positive value of $t$ (in seconds, to four significant figures) at which it occurs. (c) Find the two values of $t$ in $0\leq t<0.02$ at which $V(t)=5$, to four significant figures.
questions.answer: (a) $R=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=\sqrt{100}=10$. $\alpha=\arctan\left(\dfrac{8}{6}\right)\approx0.9273$ rad. So $V(t)=10\sin(100\pi t+0.9273)$. (b) The maximum voltage is $R=10$ volts, occurring when $100\pi t+0.9273=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, i.e. $t=\dfrac{1.5708-0.9273}{100\pi}\approx0.002049$ s. (c) Solve $10\sin(100\pi t+0.9273)=5\Rightarrow\sin(100\pi t+0.9273)=0.5$. Using $100\pi t+0.9273=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\approx2.6180$: $t=\dfrac{2.6180-0.9273}{100\pi}\approx0.005382$ s. Using $100\pi t+0.9273=\dfrac{\pi}{6}+2\pi\approx6.8068$: $t=\dfrac{6.8068-0.9273}{100\pi}\approx0.01872$ s.
